readme.html:
ae-agent-skills

An offline-first After Effects workflow built on py-aep. Version 0.14 replaces the installed legacy declarative and mutation skills with one compact skill that edits .aep files as Python object graphs.

Japanese documentation: README.ja.md

Install

npx --yes ae-agent-skills@latest install --agent codex

Replace codex with gemini, claude, or all. Restart After Effects after extension installation and open Window > Extensions (Beta) > ae-agent-skill when live verification is needed.

Example request:

Use $aftereffects-py-aep to edit /path/to/input.aep, save a new
/path/to/output.aep, reparse it, and verify the intended changes.

The workflow:

  • parses once, applies all edits in memory, and saves once;
  • never overwrites the input project;
  • reparses the output and checks semantic assertions;
  • uses the live AE bridge only for rendering, expression diagnostics, visual bounds, installed fonts/effects, open-project runtime state, and independent animation checks;
  • records production feedback in the bundled feedback template.

The pinned py-aep 0.19.0 includes upstream fixes for the keyframe timing and easing bugs reproduced in 0.15.1. Continue native verification, including save/reopen, before animation signoff. See the reproduction and exceptional fallback.

Generative graphics from code

Code-authored HTML/Canvas/SVG/WebGL animation is a core feature of the existing aftereffects-py-aep skill. Render local, frame-addressable code to a PNG sequence and import it into an AEP alongside native layers, text, and effects. No additional AE plugin is required. The result is raster footage, not AE-native shapes; edit the archived source and rerender to change its pixels.

ae-generative render /path/to/scene --output /path/to/new-render

The installer creates a dedicated Python environment under ~/.local/share/ae-agent-skills/, including py-aep, Playwright, and Chromium. It does not use pip --user or modify Homebrew/system Python packages. Python 3.10+ with venv and Node.js 18+ are required. Add the launcher directory to your shell PATH:

export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/ae-agent-skills/bin:$PATH"
# Run task-specific py-aep scripts with the same managed interpreter:
"$HOME/.local/share/ae-agent-skills/bin/python" /path/to/task.py

The same bin directory provides ae-cli and ae-generative. You can call these by their full paths without changing PATH. Close/reopen your agent after changing PATH. Existing pip-installed CLI copies are left untouched, so put this directory before older Python bin directories.

A failed package upgrade leaves the previous environment selected. A failed browser download still installs the CLI and skill, but reports that browser setup is incomplete. Retry with ae-generative setup, or rerun the installer with --skip-extension. --skip-cli skips the Python environment and browser entirely. Pip/skill-only users must create their own venv and install Chromium with that same interpreter.

Full installation and live AE verification target macOS. Linux supports the offline Python/browser workflow with --skip-extension, but may need Playwright's OS libraries. The npm installer does not support Windows. Initial setup needs network access to GitHub, PyPI and Playwright's browser downloads; rendering uses local assets only. Allow roughly 1 GB for a fresh environment/browser, plus PNG sequences and retained older upgrade environments. Browser binaries are downloaded, not bundled in npm/ZXP. See third-party licenses.

Missing managed Chromium is an error; another browser is only used when explicitly selected with --browser. Reproducibility requires the same browser/runtime, fonts, and local inputs. Only execute trusted local code.

See the generative workflow for the manifest, frame API, source archive, alpha support, and py-aep import helper.

Migration from 0.13

Version 0.14 installs aftereffects-py-aep in place of the previous declarative and mutation skills. The live CLI remains available for focused runtime verification. Task scripts and projects are not migrated or rewritten automatically.

To return to the older workflow, remove the installed aftereffects-py-aep skill and install the explicit version ae-agent-skills@0.13.0; latest now uses py-aep.

skills.name: aftereffects-cli
skills.description: Command-by-command After Effects editing and inspection via ae-cli, including PNG snapshots, comp-layer assembly, footage cuts, audio changes, whole-layer text styling, and visual-bounds alignment or distribution. Best for surgical edits, visual verification, and debugging of existing scenes.

skills.name: aftereffects-declarative
skills.description: Primary After Effects workflow using ae-cli apply-scene with declarative JSON (composition/assets/comp layers/footage cuts/audio/text styles/layout/layers/animations/expressions/parent/repeater/effect params). Use this by default for composition building and repeatable footage, audio, text, or visua

skills.name: aftereffects-py-aep
skills.description: Edit, inspect, create, and validate After Effects .aep projects offline with py-aep, without opening After Effects for file-level work. Use for existing AEP template edits, composition/layer/property/keyframe/text/shape/footage/render-queue changes, batch processing, new AEP creation, or code-author
